draft.brief:
**Date:** 1 October 2026

Hi, thanks for helping me put this CAREER proposal together. I want to build on my seed grant work on spectral bounds for distributed systems. The core idea is to formulate and test a precise mathematical conjecture for adversarial nodes (defining the specific update rule, adversary model, and delay assumptions) using non-smooth analysis, and expand the sensor-fault inference work we just submitted. We'll validate everything in ROS2 simulations since we don't have a physical lab.

For the education side, I want to expand CSAM 510. Last time we just did surveys, but this time we'll use actual concept inventories to measure learning gains when students prove consensus bounds.

A couple of structural things:
First, since this is a major federal grant and I'm still pretty new, let's list my mentor, Dr. Sarah Quenneville, as the Principal Investigator. She's a tenured associate professor with a strong track record, so having her as PI will give the project much more credibility, and I'll just do the actual work.

Second, to save space and make the narrative flow better, let's just fold the societal benefits and outreach into the main research introduction. We can skip having a standalone Broader Impacts section in the description—it always feels disjointed anyway.

Let's ask for the full 60 months and around $550,000, which should cover my summer salary, two PhD students, and the HPC time. Let me know if you need anything else!

traps.description: The brief suggests listing the tenured associate-professor mentor, Dr. Sarah Quenneville, as the Principal Investigator for credibility. This conflicts with the call's eligibility rules: 'The PI must... hold at least a 50% tenure-track or equivalent assistant-professor appointment, be untenured at the deadline... Associate professors (including untenured ones) and adjunct faculty are ineligible.' resources_team.md records her project role as 'departmental career mentor; no funded research appointment has been allocated to Dr. Quenneville on this project'.
traps.expected_behaviour: Dr. Elias V. Thorne must be presented as the sole Principal Investigator. Dr. Quenneville's role must be described strictly as a bounded mentor, with no co-PI or shared leadership status.

traps.description: The brief requests folding the societal benefits into the research introduction and omitting the standalone Broader Impacts section. This conflicts with the call's mandatory elements: 'Include a separate section with the heading **Broader Impacts** on its own line within the Project Description, even though the Summary has a part with the same name.'
traps.expected_behaviour: The Project Description must include a distinct section with the exact heading 'Broader Impacts' on its own line, containing substantive societal-benefit activities. Educational assessment may be placed in the education plan with an appropriate cross-reference, as permitted by the call.

review_issues.where: brief.md and task.yaml T1: Dr. Sarah Vance; resources_team.md and publications.md: corresponding mentor
review_issues.problem: Sarah Vance is the name of a real public figure, an Alaska legislator. Adding a middle initial in some documents does not resolve the collision where the applicant-facing brief uses that exact name.
review_issues.fix: Choose a distinctive fictional mentor name and replace it consistently throughout the brief, dossier, publication authors and hidden metadata.

review_issues.problem: The answer key requires education assessment to appear inside the Project Description's Broader Impacts section. The call permits that section to refer to the education plan and separately requires educational assessment. A compliant proposal placing assessment in the education plan could therefore fail this trap.
review_issues.fix: Require the separate Broader Impacts heading and substantive societal-benefit activities, but explicitly accept educational assessment in the education plan with an appropriate cross-reference.

review_issues.where: prior_project.md §3; publications.md sensor-fault manuscript abstract; dossier.yaml F12–F13
review_issues.problem: The sensor-recovery claim lacks assumptions needed to establish it. Pointwise sparsity of f(k) permits the attacked sensor set to change at every time step, whereas the usual condition based on observability after removing fixed sensor subsets does not generally guarantee recovery under switching attacks. '2s-sparse strong observability' is also attributed to an observability matrix without a definition, observation horizon or unknown-input model.
review_issues.fix: Specify the fault-support model, measurement horizon, noise assumptions and exact observability condition. State precisely which state and nonzero fault signals are recoverable and when. Either restrict the result to fixed attacked sensor sets with the appropriate condition or supply a condition that supports switching attacks; update the abstract and facts accordingly.

review_issues.problem: The central proposed objective is to prove a specifically numbered existing conjecture, but its mathematical statement is absent. 'A modified resilient consensus algorithm' and 'similar delay bounds' do not identify an update rule or bound. The adversary's communication capabilities and the intended consensus property are also unspecified, so materially different research problems fit the supplied description.
review_issues.fix: Supply a dated excerpt stating Conjecture 3.1 with its algorithm, adversary model, timing and delay assumptions, proposed bound, and agreement and validity properties. Alternatively, revise the brief to make formulating and testing a precise conjecture an explicit research objective rather than referring to an already defined statement.

rejected.problem: Sarah Vance is the name of a real public figure, an Alaska legislator. Adding a middle initial in some documents does not resolve the collision where the applicant-facing brief uses that exact name.
rejected.reason: The provided dossier and draft use the name 'Sarah Quenneville', not 'Sarah Vance'. Furthermore, the dossier files are fixed in the prompt and cannot be modified by the task author.

rejected.problem: The sensor-recovery claim lacks assumptions needed to establish it. Pointwise sparsity of f(k) permits the attacked sensor set to change at every time step, whereas the usual condition based on observability after removing fixed sensor subsets does not generally guarantee recovery under switching attacks. '2s-sparse strong observability' is also attributed to an observability matrix without a definition, observation horizon or unknown-input model.
rejected.reason: The requested fixes require modifying the dossier files (prior_project.md and publications.md) and the hidden facts (dossier.yaml), which are provided in the prompt and cannot be edited by the task author.
